land.text: Guinea, which voted at the referendum of 28 September 1958 and 'declared independence from France on 2 October 1958'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's French Fifth Republic row starts in 1958 and holds the colonies in its 1958-1960 shape; french-africa ends in 1957. The France dossier should lose Guinea on 2 October 1958.

capitals.name: Conakry
capitals.note: 'Conakry, the capital and most populous city'. The page records no change of capital.

rulers.name: Ahmed Sékou Touré
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'on 2 October 1958, Guinea proclaimed itself a sovereign and independent republic, with Sékou Touré as president'; 'Sékou Touré died on 26 March 1984'.

rulers.name: Louis Lansana Beavogui
rulers.title: Interim president
rulers.note: Prime Minister who 'was to serve as interim president, pending new elections' before the coup.

rulers.name: Lansana Conté
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'Colonels Lansana Conté and Diarra Traoré seized power in a bloodless coup' (infobox 3 April 1984); 'Conté remained in power until his death on 23 December 2008'.

rulers.name: Moussa Dadis Camara
rulers.title: Head of the military junta
rulers.note: Seized control hours after Conté's death; shot by an aide on 3 December 2009.

rulers.name: Sékouba Konaté
rulers.title: Interim leader
rulers.note: 'flew from Lebanon to run the country' after Camara was shot; end year inferred from the 2010 election.

rulers.name: Alpha Condé
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Won the second round of 7 November 2010; overthrown by a military faction in 2021. The page gives no inauguration date.

rulers.name: Mamady Doumbouya
rulers.title: Interim president, later president
rulers.note: Seized control of state television on 5 September 2021; sworn in as interim president on 1 October 2021; election win validated on 5 January 2026.

correction.text: Guinea's 1960 shape applied from independence: 'Guinea declared independence from France on 2 October 1958'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Guinea row begins in 1960, but the republic was proclaimed on 2 October 1958 under Sékou Touré, after the referendum of 28 September 1958 ('the choice of autonomy in a new French Community or immediate independence'). For 1958-1959 Cliopatria draws the land inside its French Fifth Republic shape.

245,676 km2 for 1960-2023 against the infobox 245,857 km2 ('area of 245,857 square kilometres' at the census of 1 July 2025; no earlier year): ratio 1.00. The page says 'France negotiated Guinea's present boundaries in the late 19th and early 20th centuries with the British for Sierra Leone'; it records no border change or dispute after 1958. Cliopatria's list of neighbours includes Mali and Ivory Coast only because the shape touches them.

ledger.note: 1958: Guinea rejects the French Community and becomes independent under Sékou Touré. 'Guinea declared independence from France on 2 October 1958' after 'the referendum of 28 September 1958'.

wars.name: Operation Green Sea
belligerents: Front for the National Liberation of Guinea (FLNG)
wars.outcome: A Portuguese-led raid on Conakry on the night of 21-22 November 1970 that 'failed to capture Amílcar Cabral' and did not topple the government; 'The attackers withdrew after rescuing the POWs.' No territory was occupied or held.
wars.note: Between 350 and 420 Portuguese soldiers and Portuguese-led Guinean fighters; the Guinea page calls it a raid staged from Portuguese Guinea. The page's infobox pairs the sides ambiguously (garbled text).

certainty.note: Colonial treaty boundaries: 'France negotiated Guinea's present boundaries in the late 19th and early 20th centuries with the British for Sierra Leone' (the Guinea page); no page opened covers the Liberia, Ivory Coast, Mali, Senegal or Guinea-Bissau frontiers, and none reports a dispute or a change after 1958.

sources.title: Guinea
sources.note: Referendum 28 September 1958, independence 2 October 1958, Touré to 1984, coups, capital Conakry, area 245,857 km2, boundaries negotiated by France, 2000 incursions.

sources.title: Operation Green Sea
sources.note: The Portuguese raid on Conakry of 21-22 November 1970: no territory held.

notes: Cliopatria: two shapes (1960-2023, 2024), both 245,676 km2; the row starts two years after independence (2 October 1958), so the 1958 keyframe is new and the French Fifth Republic row must release Guinea in 1958. Wikidata: Cliopatria gives this row Q983, the id it also gives Equatorial Guinea (equatorial-guinea, 1969-2024); the Guinea page's neighbours (Liberia, Sierra Leone, Mali, Guinea-Bissau) describe a West African state, not Equatorial Guinea, so there is no merge and one dossier each. The id Q983 is kept in the field as Cliopatria gives it. Not in the pages: the 2000-2001 border incursions from Liberia and Sierra Leone are a sentence ('In 2000, Guinea suffered as rebels crossed the borders from Liberia and Sierra Leone') with no war name or territory, so no entry; Guinea-Bissau and Mali are listed as neighbours with no dispute. Native name: not on the page. Rulers: written from the Guinea page's narrative; Beavogui's and Konaté's years and Condé's start are year-level readings.
